published_comparison_source.authors: Zarina Estrada Fernández and Aarón Grageda Bustamante
published_comparison_source.chapter: La historiografía lingüística como ejercicio disciplinario compartido: la obra de Matthäus Steffel
published_comparison_source.book: Las lenguas de México. Diálogos historiográficos
published_comparison_source.publisher: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, Instituto de Investigaciones Bibliográficas
published_comparison_source.note: The chapter explicitly compares Steffel color terms with Hilton 1959 and Brambila 1976.

estrada_grageda_interpretation.historical_color_derivation: Steffel color forms contain derived endings described by the authors as -game, -came or -queme.
estrada_grageda_interpretation.continuity_statement: The authors explicitly note that these forms persist in data from Brambila and Hilton.
estrada_grageda_interpretation.hilton_variation_note: The chapter comments on -nami/-cami alternation in Hilton color terms.
estrada_grageda_interpretation.burgess_note_reported_by_chapter: Burgess analyzes -ka in -kame as augmentative joined to participial -ame.

caballero_2022_context.agentive_past_kame: Caballero documents -kame in past agentive nominalizations and notes a Guarijío diachronic analysis -ka/-ga + -ame.
caballero_2022_context.adjectival_relative_analysis: Caballero treats -ame and -kame as suppletive participial allomorphs without tense distinctions in adjectival/relative-clause uses.
caballero_2022_context.importance: Modern -kame belongs independently to a participial domain, but its internal history/order is not assumed to be identical to Steffel -ameke.

historical_merrill_context.steffel_ameke_chain: Merrill analyzes relevant historical chains with participial -(a)me plus optional final reduplicative -kV/-ke.
historical_merrill_context.structural_warning: Steffel -ame-ke and modern -ka/-k-ame analyses have different morpheme ordering in the published accounts; do not collapse them into one automatic sound change.

research_consequence: The color domain provides an independently published multi-source bridge from Steffel -ameke-type forms to Hilton -ami and Brambila -kame forms. It substantially strengthens the diachronic research program while simultaneously showing that the relevant participial morphology may have multiple historical/allomorphic structures rather than a single linear -ameke > -ami pathway.

candidate_updates.reason: Estrada and Grageda independently publish the exact Steffel tschocámeke ~ Hilton chócami ~ Brambila chókame comparison. SRC-02 Chócami remains classified Adj, so source-explicit Pp status in SRC-02 is still not claimed.
